narrative.overview:
Junto is a dark room lit by one warm lamp. The operator sits at a canvas of agent seats, task boards and regions, and the room stays quiet until something needs them. AGENTS.md says it plainly: "The UI exists to show what needs the operator: the seat's state ring and halo, the inbox, notifications and sound cues." Everything else stays out, because every extra surface competes for attention. The lamp is amber, the home hue, and it is almost the only light in the room: about 95 percent of colored marks are amber, with sparse cyan for focus and keys, and crimson kept for blockers alone.

The voice is an instrument panel, not a dashboard. Type is monospace by default (the root font is `--font-mono`), small and dense: most of the app reads at 10, 11 and 12px, on 28px rows. A condensed display face stamps titles, the wordmark and the label node in uppercase with wide tracking. Strokes are hairlines of ink at low alpha, never greys. Depth in dark comes from small steps in surface lightness, not from shadows. The bright theme is a designed daylight edition on warm paper, never a mechanical inversion.

This system rejects: cards with action buttons on them, decorative motion, gradients and blur shadows on canvas nodes, color as the only carrier of state, generic robot glyphs where a seat's portrait belongs, and operator copy that explains mechanics (ports, grants, masks, wire families). Canvas nodes are not cards at all: a node is one chip with its contents hanging from a thin spine, and the ground shows through (`docs/node-card-language.md`).

Tokens have one source, `src/shared/theme/` (OKLCH primitives in `primitives.ts`, meaning per mode in `semantic.ts`), projected by `scripts/theme-build.ts` into `src/renderer/styles/theme.generated.css` with `bun run theme:build`. Runtime consumers (canvas paint, inline styles) read the same source through `src/renderer/lib/theme.ts` (`HUE`, `HUE_TEXT`, `INK`, `DIM`).
keyCharacteristics: Warm near-black ground, never pure black; warm paper in bright, never pure white.
One home hue (amber), one focus hue (cyan), one alarm hue (crimson).
Monospace instrument type at a six-step scale from 10 to 24px.
Hairline ink strokes and ink-alpha overlays for every hover, tint and divider.
Flat surfaces; shadows only on floating frames above the canvas.
Status is a shape plus a word, never color alone.
Motion runs on the compositor and is never slowed to save frames.

rules.name: The Lamplight Rule
rules.body: About 95 percent of the colored marks on any screen are amber. Cyan is for focus and keys. Everything else is ink. If a screen has three hues competing, two of them are wrong.

rules.name: The Crimson Means Blocked Rule
rules.body: Crimson marks a blocker, a failure, a refusal or a destructive action. It is never a brand accent, a highlight or a decoration.

rules.name: The Mark and Word Rule
rules.body: A hue drawn as a mark (dot, glyph, ring, border) uses its base token; a hue drawn as text uses its `-fg` token (`amber-fg`, `cyan-fg`, `crimson-fg`, `label-<name>-fg`). The marks fall near 3 to 1 on paper; the words clear 4.5 to 1.

rules.name: The One Source Rule
rules.body: Never hardcode a palette hex, rgba or OKLCH value in a component. Edit `src/shared/theme/`, run `bun run theme:build`, and consume the token (`lint:design-tokens` holds it). There is never a second palette.

rules.name: The Six Steps Rule
rules.body: New work uses exactly six sizes: `label` 10px, `body` 11px, `body-lg` 12px, `title` 14px, `display` 18px, `hero` 24px. `micro` 8px and `caption` 9px are legacy and under review: never reach for them in new work. There is no 13px. A raw pixel size is a defect waiting for its nearest step (`scripts/design-token-codemod.ts` holds the mapping).

rules.name: The Instrument Type Rule
rules.body: Mono is the default voice. The display face is a stamp: uppercase, tracked, short. The prose face is for paragraphs a person wrote. Never set a control, a count or a node name in the prose face.

rules.name: The Attention Rule
rules.body: A surface exists only if it shows something that needs the operator. Seat internals (sessions, notes, transcripts, plumbing) never get a surface, because every extra surface competes for attention.

rules.name: The Flat Canvas Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the canvas casts a blurred shadow. A node lifts 1px on hover with `transform`, and that is all the depth it gets.

rules.name: The Three Layers Rule
rules.body: Every overlay belongs to exactly one system: base (canvas, tabs, dock, bars), working (terminals, focus views, settings, dialogs from them) or operator (Cmd+K search, the Cmd+I needs-you feed, the agent switcher, above everything). A z-index of 100 or more is one of the `--layer-*` tokens (`lint:layers`), and an overlay renders through its layer's shell, never a hand-rolled portal or backdrop.

rules.name: The Whole Border Rule
rules.body: A border that carries state or a hue goes all the way round. State changes the whole border's color, the fill or the weight; it never paints one side. The only one-sided lines are neutral structure: layout dividers and the `stroke-hi` node spine, which never change color with state.

rules.name: The House Focus Ring Rule
rules.body: Keyboard focus is one mark everywhere: 2px of full-strength `cyan`. Outside with a 2px offset where there is room (`FOCUS_OUTLINE` in `src/renderer/components/ui/focus.ts`), inset as a 2px shadow where a clipping parent would cut it (`FOCUS_RING_INSET`). Canvas nodes ring the head chip at a 3px offset in screen pixels at every zoom. Selection (the 1px amber ring) and focus (the cyan outline) are always distinct. Only `src/renderer/lib/focus-ownership.ts` moves focus.

rules.name: The No One-Sided Edge Rule
rules.body: Never mark state with one colored edge: no colored left, right, top or bottom border, no stripe, no one-side inset shadow on a selected row, a tab, a card or a callout. Show state with a full border, a background tint, weight, or an icon. A selected row is an `overlay-2` tint, as in Cmd+K. A callout is a full 1px border in its hue at about 30 percent plus a tint at about 8 percent. Neutral hairline dividers and quote rules are structure, not state, and stay. A colored one-side line that is not state on a row, card or callout is kept by name: the text caret, a spinner arc, a link or mention underline. `tests/one-sided-accent-border.test.ts` is the lock.

rules.name: The Copy Law
rules.body: No middle dot (U+00B7) on any surface: product copy, UI strings, generated documents, artifacts. Separate with commas, em dashes or spaces. Derived wire sentences read as spoken compounds ("access stops", "watch completes").

rules.name: The Motion Law
rules.body: Never slow, step, throttle or still a moving animation anyone can see to save frames, GPU or power. Motion runs on the compositor: seat rings turn and pulse every display frame with `transform` and `opacity` only, still parts baked once into the atlas (`src/renderer/lib/activity-atlas.ts`). Motion no one can see (hidden window, reduced motion, a ring under an opaque surface or off screen) may stop. Only the operator changes motion. `tests/motion-law.test.ts` is the lock.

dos: Do show a selected row with the `overlay-2` tint and a hovered row with `overlay-1`.
Do build a callout as a full 1px border in its hue at 30 percent plus the same hue at 8 percent fill.
Do pair every status color with a shape and a word: triangle Blocked, filled circle Needs you, open arc Working, hollow circle Off.
Do use the six type steps (10, 11, 12, 14, 18, 24px) and the mono voice by default.
Do draw hues as text with their `-fg` token and as marks with their base token.
Do keep state transitions at 120 to 220ms on an exponential ease out (`cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` is the house curve).
Do give every button at least a 24px hit height and every control the 2px cyan focus ring.
Do render overlays through their layer's shell (`FocusSurface`, `Dialog`, `Popover`, `Dropdown`, `OperatorModalShell`) and stack with `--layer-*` tokens.
Do draw a seat with its portrait wherever it is named.
Do design bright as its own daylight edition on warm paper, with its own values in `semantic.ts`.
donts: Don't put a colored left, right, top or bottom border, a stripe, or a one-side inset shadow on a selected row, card, tab or callout.
Don't use a middle dot (U+00B7) anywhere, in copy, UI strings, docs or artifacts.
Don't slow, step, throttle or still visible motion, and don't animate a ring with anything but `transform` and `opacity`.
Don't use `micro` (8px) or `caption` (9px) in new work, and don't introduce a 13px or any raw pixel size.
Don't put action buttons ("open", "stop", "detach", form CTAs) on a canvas node.
Don't use crimson for anything but blockers, failures, refusals and destructive actions.
Don't let color alone carry status.
Don't use pure black or pure white for a surface, or a grey for a stroke; strokes are ink at alpha.
Don't hardcode a hex, rgba or OKLCH value in a component, or add a second palette.
Don't give a canvas node a blur shadow or a gradient.
Don't add a backdrop, a window Escape listener or a raw z-index of 100 or more to a surface.
Don't use a native select, JSX `autoFocus`, or a generic robot glyph for a seat.
Don't explain mechanics in operator copy: no ports, grants, masks, compiles or wire families. Say what the operator can do, or say nothing.
Don't put two primary amber buttons on one surface.
